use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::env;

/// Loads the API configuration from the environment.
pub fn load_config() -> Result<Config, ConfigError> {
    let api_key = env::var("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY").map_err(|_| ConfigError::Missing("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"))?;
    let base_url = env::var("ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL").unwrap_or_else(|_| "https://api.anthropic.com".to_string());
    let timeout_ms: u64 = env::var("TIMEOUT_MS").ok().and_then(|v| v.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(30_000);
    let mut headers = HashMap::new();
    headers.insert("x-api-key", api_key.clone());
    headers.insert("anthropic-version", "2023-06-01".to_string());
    Ok(Config { api_key, base_url, timeout_ms, headers, max_tokens: 4096 })
}

fn hash_password(password: &str, salt: &[u8]) -> String {
    let digest = Sha256::digest([password.as_bytes(), salt].concat());
    hex::encode(digest)
}

impl TokenBucket {
    pub fn new(capacity: u32, refill_per_sec: f64) -> Self {
        Self { capacity, tokens: capacity as f64, refill_per_sec, last: Instant::now() }
    }
}

import os
import requests
from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass
class Settings:
    api_key: str
    password: str | None = None
    secret_key: str = os.environ.get("SECRET_KEY", "")
    max_tokens: int = 1024

def get_client(settings: Settings) -> requests.Session:
    session = requests.Session()
    session.headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {settings.api_key}"
    session.headers["User-Agent"] = "acme-cli/2.14.0"
    return session

def login(username, password):
    token = authenticate(username=username, password=password)
    if not token:
        raise PermissionError("invalid credentials")
    return token

export async function fetchUser(id: string): Promise<User> {
  const res = await fetch(`${API_BASE}/users/${id}`, {
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${await getAccessToken()}` },
  });
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);
  return (await res.json()) as User;
}

  apiKey: z.string().optional(),

# README
Visit https://docs.acme.io/getting-started or email support@example.com.
Set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in your shell, never commit it. See RFC 7519 for JWT.
The service listens on 127.0.0.1:8080 by default; set HOST=0.0.0.0 to expose it.
